name: Hair fibers

lead: Hair fibers are tiny colored keratin or cotton strands, sold as a powder in a shaker, that cling to existing hair by static charge. They are used to fill in thinning areas and the part so scalp visibility drops within a minute.

They are among the most widely used camouflage tools for men and women with early to moderate hair loss. Survey and cross-sectional studies report high satisfaction, and no clinical measurement of hair growth is claimed, since the effect is purely visual.

paras: The fibers carry an electrostatic charge that makes them bond to hair shafts, adding apparent width and covering skin between hairs. A hairspray or fixing mist is typically applied to lock them in place until the next wash.

Risks are low: rare scalp itching, and fibers can run in rain or sweat or rub onto pillows and collars. They do not stop hair loss and work poorly in areas with no hair to grip, including scarred zones. Evidence is limited to satisfaction surveys and small studies, but the effect on appearance is obvious, which is why the rating is strong for cosmetic use.
